## Install — no GitHub CLI, no tokens, no SSH keys

Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract, and run the bundled installer. Same flow on every OS.

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
cd jtr-0.10.0
./install.sh
```

**Windows**
```powershell
cd .\jtr-0.10.0\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then runs `uv tool install` on the extracted source. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/BD-AI-SDLC/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for manual steps and troubleshooting.

## What's new

**jtr supports Jira Cloud.** Until now a `*.atlassian.net` base URL was rejected at `jtr init` — deliberately, because jtr spoke only the Server/DC REST dialect and a Cloud URL would otherwise have failed later with an opaque 401. Both deployments are now supported, and the deployment is detected from the base URL.

The two dialects differ in more places than the version number in the path, so rather than sprinkle `if cloud:` through the client, the whole divergence lives in one module and everything else follows from it:

| | Server / Data Center | Cloud |
|---|---|---|
| Auth | PAT (Bearer), or browser SSO | Account email + API token (Basic) |
| Setup | `jtr auth pat` / `jtr auth sso` | `jtr auth token` |
| Search paging | `--start-at` (offsets, with a total) | `--cursor` (tokens, no total) |
| `jtr assign` takes | a username | an email, display name, or accountId |

### Cloud setup

```bash
jtr init --base-url https://your-tenant.atlassian.net
jtr auth token          # prompts for email + API token
```

Create the API token at <https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens>.

### The details

- **Detection is a hostname guess, and says so.** If yours misleads — a Cloud tenant on a vanity domain, or a self-hosted instance on a Cloud-shaped name — pin it with `jtr config deployment server|cloud|auto` or `jtr init --deployment cloud`. `jtr config show` reports which dialect the config targets, and `--json` gained `deployment` and `api_version`.
- **Auth methods are validated against the deployment.** `sso`/`pat` are Server/DC and `token` is Cloud; asking for one that can't work is refused up front rather than deferred to a confusing 401. `jtr auth sso` on Cloud explains that Atlassian doesn't accept browser session cookies as REST credentials, instead of opening a browser that can't help. Cloud has exactly one workable method, so `jtr init` doesn't ask which to use.
- **Paging is explicit per dialect.** Cloud's `/search/jql` endpoint (which replaced the removed `/search`) pages by opaque cursor and reports no total. Passing `--start-at` on Cloud or `--cursor` on Server/DC is an `unsupported_option` error rather than a silent page one. Under `--json`, Cloud reports `"total": null` with a `next_page_token` to feed back via `--cursor`; the table view prints `N ticket(s)` instead of `N of M`.
- **`jtr assign` takes a human identifier on Cloud.** The API identifies people by opaque `accountId`, so an email or display name is looked up for you; `--account-id` skips the lookup when you already hold the id. A name matching several accounts is reported as `ambiguous_user` rather than guessed at.
- **`JTR_API_VERSION`** forces REST v2 or v3 and normally stays unset. It is deliberately not asked about at init: v3 doesn't exist on Server/DC, and on Cloud its only real difference is ADF-formatted comment bodies, which this CLI has no use for. It's an escape hatch, not a setting to tune.

**Also in this release:** a test suite — 81 tests covering the dialect table, both client dialects, config/auth resolution, and the CLI surface.

## Upgrading

Install as usual. Existing Server/DC setups keep working unchanged: detection resolves a self-hosted URL to `server`, which is what jtr already did, and no config, cookie, or `.env` change is required.

Every change is additive. Two shape changes are worth knowing if you already parse `--json`:

- `list mine` and `search` gained `has_more` and `next_page_token` alongside the existing `start_at`, `max_results`, `total` and `next_start_at`. `has_more` is the deployment-agnostic one — a paging loop written against it works on both. On Cloud, `total` and `next_start_at` are `null`.
- `config show --json` (and the same object returned by `init` and the `auth` commands) gained `deployment`, `api_version` and `email`. `whoami --json` gained `account_id`; its existing `key` falls back to the accountId on Cloud.

New `.env` keys — `JTR_EMAIL`, `JTR_DEPLOYMENT`, `JTR_API_VERSION` — are all optional; see `.env.example`.
